blocks.text: 3 killed in attack on Meitei villagers in India's Manipur state
At least three people were killed when suspected militants alleged to be from the ethnic Kuki community opened fire on 14 villagers from the Meitei community in India's northeastern state of Manipur.
The Meitei villagers were cutting and transporting firewood when the alleged attack took place, Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo, a senior police official, told reporters.
"Three individuals succumbed to bullet injuries. Others sustained injuries and are undergoing further medical treatment," Lhatoo told Reuters.
Meitei groups have blamed "militants" from the Kuki community for the attack, while Kuki groups have denied the allegations.
India's Manipur conflict fuels demands for separate state
The incident sparked protests in the state capital, Imphal, with villagers carrying two bodies to the residence of the chief minister.

Bordering Myanmar, Manipur is home to various ethnic communities. The hilly state has witnessed ethnic violence between its mostly Hindu Meitei majority and largely Christian Kuki minority since 2023 over economic benefits and job quotas.
